clarifyAnswers.answer: Prevention and preparedness — require local facilities (gas stations, storage tanks, marinas, etc.) to have spill prevention plans and equipment on hand
clarifyAnswers.question: What is the primary focus of this oil spill ordinance?

clarifyAnswers.answer: All of the above, plus any facility within a set distance of a waterway or stormwater inlet
clarifyAnswers.question: Which facilities should this ordinance cover? This determines how broadly your prevention requirements apply.

clarifyAnswers.answer: Tie compliance to business licensing — non-compliant facilities can have permits suspended or revoked
clarifyAnswers.question: How should the municipality enforce compliance with spill prevention plans and equipment requirements?

clarifyAnswers.answer: Moderate: written response procedures, on-site containment equipment, annual employee training, and an inspection log
clarifyAnswers.question: What should a facility's spill prevention plan be required to include at minimum?

clarifyAnswers.answer: Create a shared responsibility: Fire Marshal for plan review, Code Enforcement for permit actions
clarifyAnswers.question: Which municipal office or department should be the lead administrator responsible for reviewing spill prevention plans, conducting inspections, and initiating permit actions?
